subject: Escalation coverage currency and commit slab conversation
messages:
From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@nimbus-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation coverage — initial asks

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the call earlier. We tightened up requirements and have two asks before we can progress to procurement: 1) a clearer way to convert on-call hours into a dollar-equivalent (so our finance team can model spend across regions), and 2) flexibility on unused response credits — our usage has big seasonality.

Specifically: can unused credits be split (50/50) between roll-forward to next quarter and applied as an account-level credit? Also, what does your escalation coverage look like if we want a 24/7 PagerRotation (team-swapped across UTC offsets) versus the standard Tier 1 daytime coverage?

Attached our vendor intake timeline. Happy to jump back on a quick call.

Best,
Ayesha
Procurement Manager
Nimbus Analytics

Attachment: vendor_timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation coverage — initial asks

Hi Ayesha — thanks for the clear list. I routed the questions to our pricing and ops teams; high level answers inline below and I attached a worked example SLA matrix.

1) On-call hours → $ currency: we model on-call as an annual retainer + per-incident credits. For budgeting we can present two views: a blended $/hour (based on historical incident rates) and a fixed retainer that guarantees response windows. See the attached SLA_Matrix_v3.xlsx for an example conversion (US/EU/APAC columns).

2) Unused credits split: we can do a 50/50 roll-forward / account-credit for the first two quarters of a commit term. After that we'll revert to a 25% roll-forward cap unless you increase the commit slab. This is a non-standard concession, so we will need it documented in contract language.

3) 24/7 PagerRotation: we offer a tiered escalation add-on for full 24/7 coverage; it includes a dedicated on-call handoff playbook and a named senior response engineer for Tier 2 escalations. Pricing shown per 10k qps-equivalent of traffic in the SLA matrix.

Next steps: Ben/CustOps and Vanessa/SalesOps — can you confirm operational feasibility (rostered hours and named responder SLA) and a quick cost delta so I can share a single number with Nimbus?

Thanks,
Olga
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Matrix_v3.xlsx
Attachment: Redwood_Commit_Terms.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation coverage — initial asks

Olga / Vanessa — quick ops note: 24/7 PagerRotation is doable but the cost drivers are coverage overlap (hand-off buffer) and named-responder guarantees. For a US-heavy footprint like Nimbus's accounts, expect ~1.6x the daytime retainer for full 24/7 named coverage. If they want the 50/50 split on credits for only the first two quarters, we can accept but require a commit-slab of at least $250k ARR to offset the risk.

I ran a scenario in the matrix: commit slab tiers (quarterly): 250k, 500k, 1M — higher slabs reduce the roll-forward cap and per-incident unit cost. I'll flag the specific cells in the sheet and send back.

-Ben
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@nimbus-analytics.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation coverage — initial asks

Hi Ayesha — copying Aditya (pricing) to give the simple number you can show to finance.

Itemized answer for your finance model (US region, assume steady-state monthly usage):
- Base retainer (Standard response windows, Mon-Fri daytime): $12,000/month
- Full 24/7 PagerRotation (named responder + Tier 2 handoffs): +$7,200/month (this includes overlap buffers and escalation routing)
- Per-incident credits (for severity 1 incidents): 50 credits per incident at $1.20/credit
- 50/50 split on unused credits (first two quarters) available with commit slab >= $250k ARR. After two quarters, roll-forward cap = 25% unless slab increased to >= $500k.

If they want a single blended $/month for procurement, the blended for a baseline + 24/7 + 40 incidents/year works out to ~$33k/month (blended view enclosed). If Nimbus wants the commit-slab discount ladder, the effective blended price drops by 10% at 500k and 18% at 1M.

Ayesha — can you confirm whether procurement prefers a blended monthly line item or discrete rows (retainer / incidents / credits) for your PO? That determines how we present DocuSign.

Thanks, Vanessa
Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@nimbus-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation coverage — initial asks

Thanks everyone — this is the level of detail we need. Procurement prefers discrete line items (retainer / incidents / credits) so they can allocate budgets across teams. Two quick clarifications before I route to legal: 1) For the 50/50 split, can you add a sample clause that defines "unused" precisely (do reserved credits count?) and 2) When the roll-forward cap drops after two quarters, is there a notification window (we'd like 30 days to move slabs if needed).

If you can add those to the SLA_Matrix_v3.xlsx and the Redwood_Commit_Terms.pdf, we can aim to return a redlined contract within 5 business days.

I'll wait to receive the updated matrix and the sample clause.

Best,
Ayesha
Nimbus Analytics
